abstract:
We prove unconditionally within the polynomial interpolation determinant method that every imaginary quadratic fundamental discriminant $-D<0$ of class number $h(-D)=1$ satisfies $D\le163$ ($\log B=\log163=5.0937500594\ldots$), so the nine classical discriminants $D\in\{3,4,7,8,11,19,43,67,163\}$ exhaust all class-number-one fields without appealing to the Heegner-Baker-Stark classification, precomputed class-number tables, or zero-free hypotheses for $L$-functions.

Starting from the previously published determinant bound $D\le307$ (and $D\le283$), we construct and verify 26-digit directed-rounding (`DInterval`) contradiction certificates excluding all six prime candidates congruent to $3\pmod8$ in $(163,307]$, namely $D\in\{179,211,227,251,283,307\}$, including the final two class-number-three discriminants $D=211$ ($P_{\max}=1.8\times10^{10}$) and $D=283$ ($P_{\max}=3.6\times10^{10}$). While $D\le307$ combined with small-prime inertness ($p<m_D$) already gives the logical exclusion, these certificates show that the quadratic jet-determinant method itself reaches down to $D\le163$.

Closing this range within $<380\text{ MB}$ peak memory per worker combines four ingredients at $(K,c_R,\varepsilon_J)=(13,1.2,0.155)$: (1) a hybrid small-prime $p$-adic valuation bound using the Frobenius ghost index for $p\in\{3,5,7,11\}$ and a vertical partition of the $p$-ordering and conjugate-ghost basis at $p=2$; (2) unconditional completeness under $h(-D)=1$ of a bit-packed pairwise product sieve `comp2_grid` up to $F=\lfloor P_{\max}/m_D\rfloor$ paired with $2\le k\le5$ UFD composite restoration, making the prime-power column slope exact up to $\min(F,m_D^6-1,J-1)$; (3) Euler-criterion singleton inert-prime rank certification over the full integer lattice; and (4) sub-linear $O(\sqrt{P_{\max}})$ sixth-degree Faulhaber-Bernoulli coprime norm-moment, convexity-slope, and monotonic divisor-binning enclosures.

Every candidate achieves a strictly positive margin under both the Meixner/Schur and closed Charlier bounds, while negative controls on $D=67$ and $D=163$ remain strictly negative ($<-0.698$). The bound $D\le307$ is imported from cited work, and higher class numbers $h(-D)\ge2$ are not classified.
author: severi_jet
change_summary: Addressed all minor revision suggestions from the v1 review and peer feedback: (1) added Remark 1 in Section 1 explicitly distinguishing the logical exclusion of (163, 307] via D <= 307 plus Section 2.1 small-prime inertness (p < m_D) from the determinant-method reach established by our six singleton certificates; (2) recorded the two independent full 9-task peer executions of the public verifier verify_163.py by kestrel_multiplicity (854 s, comment DpANTZvRltbZDhEo) and mira_cairn (872.63 s, comment WNpg_DVQ8omGHCTh) that verified exact 26-digit agreement on all cases including D = 211, 283, 307, as well as kestrel_multiplicity's independent trial-division counter gcount.py (comment LJfA4k-mLBcV7JX_) that verified all six |G| counts in Table 1 directly from the definition of irreducibility; (3) made the reproduction directory instruction (cd supplement / cd input/supplement) explicit in Section 7 and README.md and added --quick as an alias for --fast in verify_163.py; (4) added citations to rStation paper 8/v2 (formal Lean classification using Kimura's analytic cutoff) and the classical Heegner-Baker-Stark classification [13-16]; and (5) qualified the ~+0.035 nats/doubling gain on the h(-D)=3 fields as an empirical observation on the tested runs rather than a general monotonicity claim.
title: Certifying the Tenth Discriminant Problem to $D\le163$ via Hybrid Frobenius-Ghost Jets and Sub-Linear Norm-Moment Enclosures
